angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 634,478 km at 273.05 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 3.6623 +/- 0.0147 mas (same row, RUWE 1.05): 273.05 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.912 +/- 0.007 solar radii from Baştürk et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-4 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025MNRAS.541..714B/abstract): 634,478 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.899 +/- 0.033 solar masses from Baştürk et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-4 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025MNRAS.541..714B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5400 +/- 90 K from Bouma et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of WASP-4 b's parameter set from Bouma et al. 2019 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157..217B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bouma et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of WASP-4 b's parameter set from Bouma et al. 2019 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....157..217B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-4.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.472, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-4 (pscomppars): spectral type G8, from Triaud et al. 2010 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2010A&A...524A..25T/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, WASP-4: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-4 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.05 dex, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-4 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.17897, from Huitson et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154...95H/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-4 (pscomppars): age 7 Gyr, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-4 (pscomppars): rotation period 22.2 d, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-4 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 1.97 km/s, from Baluev et al. 2020 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020MNRAS.496L..11B/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.912 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.948. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
